slides.title: Welcome to the Bakery
slides.text: The Bakery is Tally's own workshop, and its first rule is on the wall: a share is fair only when every piece is the same size.

visual.label: The Bakery rule: a share is fair when every piece is equal

focus.cue: One cake, cut into 4 equal pieces.
Every piece is the same size: that is what fair means.

slides.title: Parts of one whole
slides.text: Cut one cake into 4 equal parts and each part is one fourth of that cake. Take 3 parts and you hold 3/4: three out of four equal parts.

visual.label: One cake cut into 4 equal parts, with 3 parts taken: 3/4

rows.label: 3/4: three out of four equal parts

focus.cue: The whole cake, cut into 4 equal parts.
Take 3 parts: that is 3/4 of the cake.

slides.title: Rough first, then place
slides.text: Rough first: 3/4 is more than half, so it sits past the middle of the line. Place it step by step.
steps: draw a line from 0 to 1 whole cake
cut the line into 4 equal parts

visual.label: 3/4 on a number line from 0 to 1 cut into fourths, past the halfway mark

focus.cue: Halfway sits at 1/2. 3/4 must land past it.
Hop 3 equal fourths from 0: past 1/4, past 1/2, and land on 3/4.

slides.title: Top counts, bottom cuts
slides.text: In 5/8, the bottom number says the whole was cut into 8 equal parts. The top number counts how many of those parts you take: 5.

visual.label: 5/8: the bottom number cuts 8 parts, the top number counts 5

focus.cue: The bottom number: the whole is cut into 8 equal parts.
The top number counts the parts you take: 5.

slides.title: Stretch: Past the whole
slides.text: The Jumble once ordered 5/4 of a cake. That is no mistake: 5 fourths is one whole cake and one more fourth.

visual.label: 5/4 of a cake: one whole cake and one more fourth

focus.cue: Four fourths make one whole cake.
One more fourth on top: 5/4 in all.

words.means: a number for a fair share of one whole
the top number: how many parts you take
the bottom number: how many equal parts the whole was cut into
one single part of a whole, like 1/4 or 1/8

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Fraction Factory at First Cuts, then serve the orders. Cut every whole into equal parts before you count any pieces.
slides.alt: Fraction Factory, First Cuts, on a phone: order 1 asks for 1/2 of a cake, and the whole cake is cut into 2 equal parts.
